title: Finite-stage detection of alteration objects and prime-to-ell generic degrees
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_a)_{a\in I}$ an inverse system of reduced affine Noetherian schemes with affine etale transition maps [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume every $S_a$ is quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], and that the inverse limit $S$ is reduced Noetherian. Fix $a_0\in I$ and a prime $\ell$ invertible on $S_{a_0}$. Let finitely many schemes $V_{b,a_0}$ of finite presentation over $S_{a_0}$, and finitely many morphisms between them, be given [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put $V_{b,a}=V_{b,a_0}\times_{S_{a_0}}S_a$ and $V_b=V_{b,a_0}\times_{S_{a_0}}S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If every $V_b\to S$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$, then there exists $a_1\geq a_0$ such that every $V_{b,a}\to S_a$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S_a$ for all $a\geq a_1$. Here the objects and maximally $\ell'$-finite morphisms are exactly those of [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]: reduced finite-type sources, all component generic points mapping to component generic points with finite residue-field extensions [def-weil-residue-field]. If any of the specified morphisms $V_b\to V_c$ are maximally $\ell'$-finite, $a_1$ may also be chosen so that all their models are maximally $\ell'$-finite for every $a\geq a_1$. Empty objects are permitted. No properness, surjectivity, covering-family, regularity, or boundary conclusion is included.

source.place: Expose III Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, printed pp.43--44, generic-degree and alteration-object permanence in its etale limit argument; compare III Proposition 3.1(i) and its finite-free generic-rank model argument, pp.37--38. Agent-formulated finite-stage interface for etale inverse systems, not the approximation-by-congruent-sections assertion of III 3.1. Finite-presentation descent is Stacks limits.tex Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation); ind-etale residue fields are separable algebraic (algebraic field-factorizations and their finite ranks descend to a finite stage).

proof.text: Restrict to $a\geq a_0$. Write $S_a=\operatorname{Spec}R_a$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, where $R=\varinjlim R_a$. Every $R_a\to R$ is flat: the later $R_b$ are flat $R_a$-modules and their ring colimit is their module colimit. Set $Q_a=Q(R_a)$ and $Q=Q(R)$. The ordinary etale total-fraction comparison gives $Q_b=Q_a\otimes_{R_a}R_b$ for $b\geq a$, and the ind-etale comparison gives $Q=Q_a\otimes_{R_a}R$. Thus $Q=\varinjlim Q_a$, and base changes of the given diagram to $\operatorname{Spec}Q_a$ have limit the diagram over $Q$. The assertion about colimits follows directly from the tensor universal property (a compatible family of balanced bilinear maps is a balanced bilinear map on the colimit). These total rings are finite products of the residue fields of the component generic points. All the $V_{b,a}$ and $V_b$ are Noetherian, since they are finite type over Noetherian bases.

source.place: Tags 01YW/01YX; Algebra Tags 00U2, 05UT, 02LX; generic-base interpretation of ILO III 6.2

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover of each $V_{b,a_0}$, and write $C_a=C_0\otimes_{R_{a_0}}R_a$ for one chart, $C=C_0\otimes_{R_{a_0}}R$ for its limit. These charts cover every model. Let $N_0$ be the nilradical of $C_0$, finitely generated because $C_0$ is Noetherian. The map $\operatorname{Spec}C_a\to\operatorname{Spec}C_0$ is etale. Its base change over $C_0/N_0$ is etale and has reduced source. Consequently $N_0C_a$ is exactly the nilradical of $C_a$: its elements are nilpotent, and its quotient is reduced. Every generator of $N_0$ maps to zero in $C$, since $V_b$ is reduced. The elementwise vanishing criterion in the ring colimit $C=\varinjlim C_a$ kills all these finitely many generators at one stage. At that stage and every later stage $N_0C_a=0$, so every chart, hence every $V_{b,a}$, is reduced. This also treats a chart with empty limit.

For each initial chart let $K_0=\ker(C_0\to C_0\otimes_{R_{a_0}}Q_{a_0})$, a finitely generated ideal of the Noetherian ring $C_0$. Flat tensor exactness and Step 1 identify its extension to $C_a$ with $K_a=\ker(C_a\to C_a\otimes_{R_a}Q_a)$, and its extension to $C$ with the analogous kernel $K$. The latter is zero: a nonzerodivisor of $R$ avoids every minimal prime of $R$, hence its image avoids every minimal prime of $C$, since $V_b/S$ is maximally dominant. As $C$ is reduced, that image is a nonzerodivisor. Localization therefore embeds $C$ into $C\otimes_RQ$. Kill the finitely many fixed generators of $K_0$ at a common stage by the elementwise colimit vanishing criterion. Then $K_a=0$ at every later stage. Every minimal prime of $C_a$ lifts along the injection $C_a\hookrightarrow C_a\otimes_{R_a}Q_a$. Its contraction to $R_a$ is minimal, because $Q_a$ is the product of precisely the generic residue fields. Thus every component generic point of every $V_{b,a}$ maps to a component generic point of $S_a$.

source.place: Tags 00EW, 00FK, 02LX, 00D6/00D7; localization and flat tensor exactness

proof.text: By the generic-fibre finiteness criterion, $V_b\times_S\operatorname{Spec}Q$ is finite over $\operatorname{Spec}Q$: on each of its finitely many field components this is the finite generic fibre of $V_b/S$. Apply finiteness descent to the system $\operatorname{Spec}Q_a$ and the finite-presentation models $V_{b,a}\times_{S_a}\operatorname{Spec}Q_a$. After one common stage, every such model is finite over $Q_a$. All schemes here are qcqs: the bases are affine, and the models have finite presentation. Finiteness persists to every later stage, since a finite algebra remains a finite module after tensor base change. Combined with Steps 2 and 3, this proves that every $V_{b,a}/S_a$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S_a$: its generic points lie in these finite generic fibres, so their residue fields are finite over those of $S_a$.

Fix one specified maximally $\ell'$-finite map. Over $Q$ write its target and source as $\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $\operatorname{Spec}D$. They are affine finite schemes by Step 4, reduced by the hypothesis, and thus finite products of finite field extensions of the field factors of $Q$. Indeed each field-factor algebra is finite-dimensional, hence Artinian, and reduced Artinian algebras are products of their residue fields. Write $1=\sum_i e_i$ for the target primitive orthogonal idempotents, so $e_iE=L_i$ is a field. For each target factor in the image, choose a source field factor $h_iD=M_i$ above it with $d_i=[M_i:L_i]$ not divisible by $\ell$, as the hypothesis permits. The corresponding idempotents satisfy $f^\#(e_i)h_i=h_i$. If the target factor is outside the image, $f^\#(e_i)=0$. These are actual idempotents of the finite generic algebras, not merely lifts modulo a nilradical. The field points here are precisely the component generic points: maximal dominance puts them over a generic point of the base and each resulting fibre is finite.

source.place: II 1.1.8, 1.1.10 and III 3.1(iii), generic finite-rank witnesses

proof.text: Let $E_a,D_a$ be the finite coordinate $Q_a$-algebras supplied by Step 4. They form scalar-base-change systems with colimits $E,D$. Lift the finitely many $e_i,h_i$ to one stage, imposing all equations $e_i^2=e_i$, $e_ie_j=0$ for $i\ne j$, $\sum e_i=1$, $h_i^2=h_i$, $f_a^\#(e_i)h_i=h_i$, and $f_a^\#(e_i)=0$ for the unhit factors, using finite-data descent, and then the elementwise vanishing criterion to impose the equations on the chosen lifts and the fixed map. They now define clopen target pieces $\operatorname{Spec}(e_iE_a)$ and source pieces $\operatorname{Spec}(h_iD_a)$ with the indicated maps. Apply fixed-degree finite-locally-free descent separately to each selected map. Its limit is $\operatorname{Spec}M_i\to\operatorname{Spec}L_i$, finite locally free of degree $d_i$. The initial maps are locally of finite presentation: they are morphisms between finite algebras over the Noetherian ring $Q_a$. Their source and target are affine, hence qcqs. Thus after enlarging the stage all selected maps have degree $d_i$, while the unhit pieces still have empty inverse image. All these equations and ranks persist under further base change.

At any later stage let $t$ be a target component generic point in the image. It lies in one of the target pieces of Step 6; that piece cannot be an unhit one, since its entire inverse image is empty. The selected source piece has fibre over $t$ a reduced finite algebra of dimension $d_i$ over $\kappa(t)$. Reducedness follows because this is a field factor restriction of the reduced finite generic algebra $D_a$: $E_a$ is a product of fields, so taking this fibre is selecting direct factors, without an additional field extension. Decompose that fibre into fields $F_j$ by the reduced Artinian product theorem. Then $d_i=\sum_j[F_j:\kappa(t)]$. Since the prime $\ell$ does not divide $d_i$, it cannot divide every summand; choose one not divisible by $\ell$. This gives the required source component generic point above $t$. Every source generic extension is finite: both source and target generic algebras are finite products of finite extensions of a common base field, and $\kappa(t)$ is an intermediate field. This proves maximal $\ell'$-finiteness at every later stage.

source.place: II 1.1.8 and III 3.1(iii), prime-to-ell degree via a finite free generic witness

proof.text: There are finitely many initial charts, objects, specified maps, and selected generic factors. Directedness gives a single upper bound $a_1$ for their stages. Every construction above persists for $a\geq a_1$, proving both assertions simultaneously. If $S$ is empty, the nonempty-limit lemma applied to the tail system shows that some $S_a$ is empty, and every later base and every model over it is empty; all assertions are then vacuous. If $S$ is nonempty but a source or target is empty, Step 4 and the finite equations in Step 6 allow zero algebras and empty factor lists, so the same argument applies. Quasi-excellence and invertibility of $\ell$ are retained hypotheses; this finite-stage interface needs neither of them beyond the setting of the parent uniformization proof.

One new statement-only ind-etale total-fraction comparison; all other facts reuse existing nodes. Statement and hypotheses retained.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q150-63cb8a67b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS: the delivery is correct and both mechanical findings are justified; no fixes. The item statement is unchanged, so the target is not weakened. I checked it against ILO II 1.1.7, II 1.1.8 (the good-degree point is required only over target points in the image), III 3.1 pp.37-38 and III 6.2 pp.43-44 ('passage à la limite'). Steps 1-8 are correct. Step 1: R_a→R is flat (05UT), Q_b=Q_a⊗R_b by the étale total-fraction node, Q=Q_a⊗R by the new node. Step 2: the nilradical N_0 is finitely generated; étale base change over C_0/N_0 has reduced source (02GO, 025O), and the generators die at one stage. Step 3: flat exactness gives K_a=K_0C_a; K=0 by 00EW plus maximal dominance; generic points then map to generic points by 00FK and 02LX. Step 4: the generic-fibre criterion, then 01ZO over the system Spec Q_a (qcqs and lft checked). Steps 5-7: idempotents carry their equations; 06AC degree d_i with lfp because finite algebras over Noetherian Q_a are finitely presented; fibres are reduced as direct factors, so some field factor has degree prime to ℓ. Step 8: 01Z2 handles empty S. New node lem-per-ind-etale-total-fraction-comparison is true by my own proof: T_A^{-1}B is a colimit of finite products of finite separable field extensions, hence reduced and zero-dimensional; its primes are exactly the minimal primes of B, so T_B is already invertible. I tested it on A=B, A→0, k[x]→k(x), an infinite separable algebraic extension and a killed factor. It is not a duplicate: the étale case is lem-sfb-etale-total-fraction-base-change and the domain case is lem-dl-a1-ind-etale-domain-generic-field. Batch-5 finding: lem-trf-finite-residue-point-closed-in-fibre is the generic fact that a point with finite residue extension is closed in its fibre, not a step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality proofs. BFS shows lem-per-generic-fibre-finiteness-criterion already lies in the nt-target-weil-conjectures closure without the item's edges (via lem-sfb-equivariant-projective-model-normalization … det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images), so the citation adds no new reach. Dropped-route finding: the item and the criterion are both on the 2026-10-19 drop list and both are now re-reached through the sfb ctf-stability Gabber chain, so nothing is revived. Neither is reached from lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve, whose finite-coefficient route lock is untouched. All ten split_report tool_uses are generic algebra or limit tools and are accepted.
